foundItems.title: 10 African Books That Take on Mental Health
foundItems.description: In Africa, mental health is something we don’t often talk about. We understand headaches. We understand stomach ulcers and other illnesses that manifest physically. But when it comes to mental health, our understanding becomes amiss. This is more apparent within African families, where many of us are not raised to talk openly about our feelings […]

foundItems.title: Cajetan Iheka’s Horizontal Comparison Takes On Comparative Literature’s “Africa Problem”
foundItems.description: What happens when African and Caribbean literature is read alongside itself, rather than continually measured against Europe and the United States? That is the question at the heart of Horizontal Comparison: Africa, the Caribbean, and the Making of Black World Literature, Cajetan Iheka’s forthcoming book from the University of Chicago Press.
